questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue operated under complete acceptance, a batch of $B$ jobs arrives and finds $m$ jobs in the system, where $K$ is the capacity level. Which condition decides whether the whole batch is admitted?
options: The batch is admitted if and only if $m+B\le K$.
The batch is admitted if and only if $m\le K-1$.
The batch is admitted if and only if $m\le K$.
The batch is admitted if and only if $m\le K-1$ and $B\le K$.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with capacity level $K$ uses complete acceptance, and batch sizes take values $B\in\{1,\dots,K_B\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B=K_B)>0$. What is the largest number of jobs that $L(t)$ can reach?
options: $K+K_B$

questions.question: In the level-crossing analysis of an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with service rate $\mu$ and stationary probabilities $\pi(n)$, at what rate is level $n$ down-crossed, that is, the number in system drops from $n+1$ to $n$, whichever batch rejection policy is used?
options: $\mu\pi(n+1)$, because jobs leave one at a time.
$\mu\pi(n)$, because the down-crossing ends at level $n$.
$\mu\mathbb{E}[B]\pi(n+1)$, because jobs leave in batches.
$\mu\sum_{k>n}\pi(k)$, since every higher state can drop below.

questions.question: Batch rejection policies in an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue and balking in a single-server queue both turn away arriving jobs. What distinguishes the two mechanisms?
options: Batch rejection always refuses whole batches, whereas balking turns away individual customers.
Batch rejection is based on the waiting time a batch faces, whereas balking uses the number in system.
Batch rejection is decided when the batch reaches the server, whereas balking is decided on arrival.
Batch rejection is decided by the system from its state, whereas under balking customers decide themselves.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with capacity level $K$, every batch contains exactly one job ($B\equiv1$). A job finds $m$ jobs in the system. How do complete acceptance, partial acceptance and complete rejection compare?
options: Complete acceptance still lets $L(t)$ reach $K+1$, while the other two policies cap it at $K$.
All three admit the job if and only if $m\le K-1$, which is blocking as in the $M/M/1/K$ queue.
Complete rejection refuses a job that finds $m=K-1$, because it requires $m+B<K$ to admit.
Partial acceptance and complete rejection coincide, but complete acceptance differs as it ignores $B$.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with capacity level $K=12$ uses partial acceptance. A batch of $B=5$ jobs arrives and finds $m=9$ jobs in the system. How many jobs of this batch are admitted?
options: $5$ jobs
$0$ jobs
$3$ jobs
$2$ jobs

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with capacity level $K=5$ uses complete rejection, and batch sizes are uniform on $\{1,2,3,4\}$. A batch arrives and finds $m=3$ jobs in the system. What is the expected number of jobs of this batch that are rejected?

An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue has capacity level $K=7$. A batch of $B=3$ jobs arrives and finds $m=4$ jobs in the system. Under which of the policies complete acceptance, partial acceptance and complete rejection is the whole batch admitted?
options: Under complete and partial acceptance only, as complete rejection needs $m+B<K$.
Under complete acceptance only, as the others see no room left when $m+B=K$.
Under complete acceptance and complete rejection; partial acceptance admits $2$.
Under all three policies, since $m\le K-1$, $\min\{B,K-m\}=B$ and $m+B\le K$.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=4$ uses complete rejection, and batch sizes are uniform on $\{1,2,3,4\}$, with $G(i)=\mathbb{P}(B>i)$. A batch arrives and finds $m=1$ job. What is the probability that it up-crosses level $n=1$, that is, takes the system from $1$ to at least $2$ jobs?

An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=1$ uses complete rejection; batches arrive at rate $\lambda_B=2$, jobs are served at rate $\mu=4$, and $\mathbb{P}(B=1)=0.6$, $\mathbb{P}(B=2)=0.3$, $\mathbb{P}(B=3)=0.1$. What is the ratio $\pi(1)/\pi(0)$ of the stationary probabilities?

For partial acceptance in an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue, the up-crossing rate of level $n<K$ is $\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{n}\pi(m)G(n-m)$, with $G(i)=\mathbb{P}(B>i)$. A student stops the sum at $m=n-1$. Which up-crossings does the student miss?
options: Those of batches that find exactly $n$ jobs, as any admitted job lifts them to $n+1$.
Those of batches that find $n+1$ jobs, as these also pass through level $n$.
None, as a batch that finds $n$ jobs starts on level $n$ and cannot cross it.
Those of single-job batches, as the term $m=n$ uses $G(0)$, which counts only them.

questions.question: Under complete acceptance in an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with Poisson batch arrivals, the long-run fraction of jobs rejected equals $\mathbb{P}(L\ge K)$. Why does the fraction of jobs, not just of batches, equal this probability?
options: Because $L(t)$ never exceeds $K$ under this policy, so $\mathbb{P}(L\ge K)=\mathbb{P}(L=K)$.
Because rate stability gives $\pi(0)=1-\rho$, which fixes the fraction of rejected jobs.
Because a rejected batch always contains a single job, so batches and jobs count alike.
Because batches find $L\ge K$ with probability $\mathbb{P}(L\ge K)$ by PASTA and the rule ignores $B$.

questions.question: In an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue under partial acceptance, with $G(i)=\mathbb{P}(B>i)$, why is the up-crossing rate of every level $n<K$ the same as in the $M^B/M/1$ queue without rejection?
options: Because batches that find fewer than $K$ jobs never lose any of their jobs.
Because rejections are rare below $K$, so ignoring them is a good approximation.
Because a batch with $B>n-m$ that finds $m\le n$ jobs still admits more than $n-m$ jobs.
Because the down-crossing rates change as well and compensate for the lost jobs.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=2$ uses complete rejection; $B$ is $1$ or $2$ with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$ each, $\lambda_B=2$ and $\mu=4$. What is the stationary probability $\pi(2)$ after normalisation?

An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=3$ uses complete acceptance; $B\in\{1,2,3\}$, $G(i)=\mathbb{P}(B>i)$, batches arrive at rate $\lambda_B$ and jobs are served at rate $\mu$. Which expression equals $\mu\pi(4)$, the down-crossing rate of level $3$?
options: $\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{2}\pi(m)G(3-m)$
$\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{3}\pi(m)G(3-m)$
$\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{2}\pi(m)G(2-m)$
$\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{2}\pi(m)G(4-m)$

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=2$ uses partial acceptance; batches arrive at rate $\lambda_B=3$ with $\mathbb{P}(B=1)=\tfrac{3}{4}$, $\mathbb{P}(B=2)=\tfrac{1}{4}$, and $\mu=4$. The stationary probability of an empty system is $\pi(0)=0.4$. What long-run fraction of the offered jobs is rejected?

In an $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with capacity level $K$ under partial acceptance, let $\pi(K)$ be the stationary probability that the system is full. How does the long-run fraction of jobs rejected compare with $\pi(K)$ when $\mathbb{P}(B\ge2)>0$?
options: It equals $\pi(K)$, since by PASTA batches find a full system with that probability.
It is below $\pi(K)$, since a batch that overflows loses only its excess jobs.
It exceeds $\pi(K)$, since batches that find $m<K$ jobs can lose their excess too.
It equals $\pi(K)$ only for $\rho<1$, and it exceeds $\pi(K)$ when $\rho\ge1$.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue under partial acceptance has load $\rho=\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[B]/\mu$. Is $\rho<1$ needed for the recursion $\mu\pi(n+1)=\lambda_B\sum_{m=0}^{n}\pi(m)G(n-m)$, $n=0,\dots,K-1$, to give a stationary distribution?
options: Yes; for $\rho\ge1$ the weights grow without bound and cannot be normalised.
No; the recursion yields $K+1$ positive weights, which always normalise.
Yes; rate stability needs $\lambda_B\mathbb{E}[B]\le\mu$ for the admitted jobs.
Yes; the check $\pi(0)=1-\rho$ still holds, so $\pi(0)>0$ forces $\rho<1$.

questions.question: An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=2$ uses complete acceptance; $B$ is $1$ or $2$ with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$ each, $\lambda_B=1$ and $\mu=2$, so the states are $0,1,2,3$. What long-run fraction of the jobs is rejected?

An $M^B/M/1/K$ queue with $K=3$ uses complete rejection; every batch has exactly $B=2$ jobs, $\lambda_B=1$, $\mu=3$, and the stationary distribution on $\{0,1,2,3\}$ is $\pi=\bigl(\tfrac{9}{17},\tfrac{3}{17},\tfrac{4}{17},\tfrac{1}{17}\bigr)$. What long-run fraction of the jobs is rejected?
